issues.title: FSST code-level LIKE filter v2: DFA over FSST codes + filter-only no-decode + segment-straddling vectors
issues.hypothesis: q13 (313ms, slowest template) spends 2.17s of operator CPU in the orders TABLE_SCAN running o_comment NOT LIKE '%unusual%packages%'. o_comment is plain FSST, and FSST registers no filter callback, so StandardColumnData::Filter (standard_column_data.cpp:76-94) falls back to decode-all and then filter. The column is filter-only, so TableScan drops the decoded strings afterwards. An implementation earlier in this run (the r10 dispatch: FSSTStorage::Filter + a KMP-chain DFA lifted to codes + a filter_only flag) measured q13 -16..-21% on the bench. EXPLAIN ANALYZE scan CPU went from 1.88s to 1.26s. The DFA itself costs only ~0.45s. About 13% of vectors cross an FSST segment boundary, so GetVectorScanType != SCAN_ENTIRE_VECTOR, and these vectors take the full-decode fallback (~0.25s, about 40% of the remaining non-DFA cost). Handling straddling vectors with the same DFA path should push q13 clearly beyond its ~14% noise band.
issues.plan: 1) Re-implement the earlier version. Add a filter_only flag to ScanFilter (src/include/duckdb/storage/table/scan_state.hpp, set in scan_state.cpp ScanFilterInfo from the TableScan projection_ids in table_scan.cpp) and mirror it into ColumnScanState before col_data.Filter in row_group.cpp (~:781). Add FSSTStorage::Filter in src/storage/compression/fsst.cpp, modelled on DictFSSTFilter (dict_fsst.cpp:180). It parses NOT?(contains|prefix|suffix|~~|!~~) with a constant pattern made only of literals and '%' (bail on '_', ILIKE and escapes) into a byte DFA (KMP chain with anchors). Per segment symbol table (cached by decoder pointer), lift it to a uint16 table trans[state][code] with escape-pending states. Run it over the vector's compressed strings, using the StringScanPartial offset and bitunpack logic, with a 4-way interleave over the lanes. NULL rows never pass. For a filter_only column, emit a constant placeholder and do not decode. Otherwise decode only the rows in sel. Any unsupported filter falls back to the existing path. 2) New in v2: in StandardColumnData::Filter, when the only failing gate is that the vector straddles a segment boundary (no updates, compression->filter on both segments, and validity has a filter or NO_VALIDITY_REQUIRED), filter piecewise. For each segment piece, call the segment's filter for the piece's row count into a temp sel, add the piece's row offset to the sel indices, and append. Advance the data and validity child states across the boundary the way ScanVector/BeginScanVectorInternal does. If that is too invasive, limit it to filter_only columns and skip the result vector entirely. 3) Tests: prefix, suffix, infix and multi-% patterns, NOT, NULLs, escape-coded bytes, a column both filtered and projected, and a vector crossing a segment boundary. Use `col||''` as a no-pushdown reference (dbe-tool sql is read-only).
issues.expected_gain: q13 -20..-28% (previous version -16..-21%, plus the ~0.25s straddle fallback removed), about -1.5..-2% geomean. Hidden templates with LIKE on FSST comment or name columns (q16 s_comment, q20 p_name 'forest%' if it is not turned into a range) gain a few %.
issues.generality: Any LIKE/contains/prefix/suffix scan filter on an FSST-compressed VARCHAR, largest where the column is only filtered. Dictionary, DictFSST and uncompressed columns are unchanged. A filtered-and-projected column with a low-selectivity predicate pays the DFA plus the decode of passing rows, which should be about even.
issues.risk: Medium-high on correctness: DFA escapes, anchors, NOT/NULL semantics, and the piecewise scan-state advance across segments in the straddle path. Performance risk is low, because unsupported cases fall back.

## Memory (gen3)

## State
- gen1: accepted JoinDependent rule order (q19), contains() selectivity (q09), perfect HJ RIGHT (q13), BF first key multi-key HJ (q09), key-set range filter through compress projs (q18), exact bitmap BF, semi-join estimate, OR-of-ranges mask, FSST simple decode + substring prefilter (q13), DELIM_GET-build BF (q22). Best 1.281x.
- gen2: E0021 deliminate SEMI + exact BF through CM offset; E0022 exact-BF small-range floor; E0023 ANTI deliminator; E0024 parallel perfect-HJ build; E0027 BitPacking per-value select + exact BF 2^27; E0029 sparse perfect-HJ exact BF; E0031 block cache 256MB + large perfect HA v3 (q13 -25%). Best 1.800x.
- gen2 r16: E0032 rare-pair substring search RETIRED (q13 -4%; FSST decode dominates).
- gen3 r1-r4: E0033 clustered-key agg, E0034 staged perfect HA sink, E0035 parallel HJ finalize 64K-1M, E0036 streaming run agg: all ACCEPTED. Best 2.120x.
- gen3 r5/r6: E0037 partition-local HJ slots RETIRED; E0038 THP >=32MB near miss. r7: E0039 THP v2 ACCEPTED. HugePageUtil in src/include/duckdb/common/huge_page_util.hpp.
- gen3 r8: E0040 coalesce sparse filtered scan chunks (<256 rows -> 1024, table_scan.cpp) ACCEPTED geomean -9.3%. Best 2.387x.
- gen3 r9: E0041 caching threshold 64->256 RETIRED (noise). Operator-output coalescing is dead after E0040.
- gen3 r10 (first attempt): the FSST DFA filter was implemented (the Claude auto-memory fsst-dfa-like-filter says q13 -16..-21%, scan CPU 1.88->1.26s, DFA only 0.45s, 13% of vectors straddle segments and fall back), but there is NO ledger entry and best is still E0040. The run was probably lost. r10 re-plan: DISPATCHED "FSST code-level LIKE filter v2" = same + piecewise filter for segment-straddling vectors in StandardColumnData::Filter (standard_column_data.cpp:76-94, gate scan_entire_vector at :88).
- If v2 is retired for a regression elsewhere: drop the straddle part (re-land v1 only). If it is retired for noise: q13 noise is ~14%, so rerun q13 alone.
- Backlog issues.md entries "Length-aware selectivity", "Perfect HJ RIGHT", "Join min/max+BF through CM", "Large perfect HA v3", "RIGHT_SEMI/ANTI join filters" have ALL LANDED (stale). Do not dispatch them. The old v1 FSST issue is superseded by v2.
- Claude auto-memory (~/.claude/.../memory) holds results from previous evolve runs AND this one. Treat them as strong priors.

## FSST filter facts
- o_comment = plain FSST (977 segs) + Constant validity; p_name FSST; p_type Dictionary. pragma_storage_info('t') shows this.
- FSST registers no `filter` callback; DictFSST has one (dict_fsst.cpp:180). StandardColumnData::Filter needs compression->filter, a validity filter (Constant validity has one) and a full vector (no segment straddle).
- row_group.cpp:757-790: filter columns go through col_data.Filter, then are Sliced by sel. TableScan drops filter-only columns via projection_ids.
- LIKE 'abc%' becomes a range ConstantFilter (zonemap), not a contains-type filter. dbe-tool sql is read-only, so use `col||''` as the no-pushdown reference.

## Per-chunk overhead (E0040 lesson)
- Sparse chunks (~14 rows) cost ~3.5us/chunk in HJ probe. Coalescing pays off below ~256 rows/chunk.
- HJ ExecuteInternal (physical_hash_join.cpp:1407) is called twice per input chunk (HAVE_MORE_OUTPUT). Small possible follow-up.

## THP facts
- THP madvise mode. Free-time MADV_DONTNEED + MADV_NOHUGEPAGE REQUIRED, or q02 +5..9%.

## Profiling trick (works, cheap)
- In one dbe-tool sql call: warm up, then `PRAGMA enable_profiling='json'; PRAGMA profiling_output='/tmp/x.json';` <query>; `PRAGMA disable_profiling;` then
  `SELECT unnest(regexp_extract_all(content, '"operator_name": "([^"]*)"|"operator_timing": ([0-9.e-]+)|"operator_cardinality": ([0-9]+)')) FROM read_text('/tmp/x.json');` Timing comes BEFORE the name. Pre-order, probe child first.
- The Bash tool allows only literal dbe-tool commands. `.timer on` as the first line. `SET disabled_optimizers='...'` for A/B.

## Hot CPU breakdowns (post-E0040)
- q09 (306ms): HJ o_orderkey=l_orderkey 0.71s (build 3.27M lineitem-side rows, probe 2.9M orders); HJ partsupp 0.38s; lineitem scan 0.58s; HASH_GROUP_BY 0.20s + CM compress proj 0.08s. Disabling CM: q09 -4% (noise), q13 0%.
- String group keys are expensive: 60M-row join+agg by (n_name, year): HASH_GROUP_BY 1.64s + CM string compress ~0.85s, vs PERFECT_HASH_GROUP_BY 0.34s for (n_nationkey, year). TryAddDictionaryGroups (aggregate_hashtable.cpp:359) handles only 1-column dictionary groups. No mechanism yet.
- q13: scan+NOT LIKE 2.17s CPU, RIGHT perfect HJ 0.34s, compress proj 0.27s, perfect HA 0.57s.
- q16: HASH_GROUP_BY 0.36s. q18 subquery agg 1.17s CPU over 60M rows/15M groups.

## Refuted (don't retry)
- VARCHAR low-cardinality group key in q09 (prior run); partition-local HJ slots; q05 join order; operator caching threshold; skipping CM wholesale.

## HJ / perfect facts
- PARALLEL_CONSTRUCT_THRESHOLD = 64K. ScanStructure::Next join_hashtable.cpp:940; NextInnerJoin:1083 uses a compaction buffer.
- Perfect HJ: perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp. Perfect HA: perfect_aggregate_hashtable.cpp, plan_aggregate.cpp. Exact BF probe: bloom_filter.cpp TemplatedLookupExact.

## Acceptance lessons
- Acceptance needs some template faster beyond noise AND a better geomean; any template slower beyond noise retires.
- Bundling or widening a near miss works (E0021, E0027, E0029, E0031, E0039).
- Full-bench single-template outliers of ±8..29% happen; rerun alone.

## Codebase facts
- Table scan loop: table_scan.cpp TableScanFunc; coalescing state in DuckTableScanState.
- CachingPhysicalOperator: physical_operator.cpp:287-470.
- HJ BF filled in JoinHashTable::InsertHashes. BitPacking Select ~bitpacking.cpp:886. TEMP tables never compressed.
- Substring prefilter: column_segment.cpp:662-860 (GetSubstringPrefilter:714). CM: src/optimizer/compressed_materialization*. Deliminator: deliminator.cpp.

## How to measure
- Bench noise: q16 ~7.9%, q18 ~5%, q13 ~14%, q09 ~8.6%, q14 ~5.1%, q05 ~20%, q04 ~20%, q07 ~13%.

## Profile snapshot (r10): q13 313, q09 306, q18 229, q16 163, q07 135, q03 130, q05 123, q04 105, q08 100, q22 94, q17 91, q19 88, q14 88, q02 53. Geomean 127.0ms.

## Dead / exhausted
- CM join-key removal, HJ prefetch, agg run-collapse, in-place finalize, FSST heap reuse, dictionary filter, scan filter cost ordering, early HT grow, sparse perfect HJ (8M range), hashed BF through CM offset, q13 eager aggregation, fused hashed BF probe, allocator flush thresholds, substring search alone, private staging for perfect HA, partition-local HJ slots, q05 join order, operator output caching threshold.

## Next candidates
1. FSST DFA v2 (dispatched r10 re-plan).
2. Low-cardinality string/multi-column group-by fast path (q09/q07/q05 n_name groups); needs a mechanism.
3. Large lineitem-side HJ builds (q09 0.71s, q07, q03): split sink vs probe cost first.
4. q18 per-group streaming-run overhead (radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp SinkInteriorRuns ~947).
5. HJ double call per input chunk (small). Skip unused local table in staged perfect HA (q13 -1..-3%).
